sources.docs/host-api.md: Controller verbs: run(value), close(), disposeChild(), snapshot(), dispose(). Injected notify(value) returns a deferred payload {value,events}; write(value) observes a state write, returned(payload) observes each operation completion. Native callback return port corresponds to the original awaited run result. Shell policy is independent from modal state; close is terminal for a modal instance.

rules.body: Apply when a deferred operation can complete after a terminal view closure, while operation completion and another consumer have independent lifetimes. README.md: "A view can receive a result while open or after it has closed; the shell belongs to the application." docs/host-api.md: "Shell policy is independent from modal state; close is terminal for a modal instance."

Check the originating modal instance's current closed state when the notification continuation executes, before assigning its value or observing a modal write. Admission-time eligibility cannot establish eligibility after suspension. TASK: "A notification received after the alerts modal is closed still updates the modal's state. Fix the issue." Original src/Workspace.jsx captures "const admitted=!s.closed;" but performs modal effects under "if(true)". Its terminal boundaries are "close(){s.closed=true;}" and "dispose(){s.closed=true;s.disposed=true;}".

Preserve the open-modal sequence of value assignment, write observation and publication. Where an injected write can synchronously close or dispose the instance, check current closure again before the remaining publication. Original src/Workspace.jsx: "s.value=result.value;env.write(s.value);void 0;publish();". Attempt 1 uses a current-state guard before assignment and another after env.write; treat the latter as a defensive checkpoint, not evidence that synchronous reentry is a documented host guarantee.

Keep original-result completion delivery outside the modal-effect guard, so closure suppresses modal effects without suppressing successful operation completion. docs/host-api.md: "write(value) observes a state write, returned(payload) observes each operation completion." It also states: "Native callback return port corresponds to the original awaited run result." Original src/Workspace.jsx places "env.returned(result);" after the modal-effect block. Preserve env.notify(input) invocation, payload identity and the existing behavior when run is invoked after close.

Limit the change to modal notification handling. TASK: "Change only the modal subscription; do not migrate the application-shell subscription." Preserve snapshot shape, terminal closure and actual unmount cleanup. Original src/Workspace.jsx: "snapshot(){return {value:s.value,closed:s.closed};}" and "useEffect(()=>()=>command('dispose',[]),[])". Do not introduce request freshness suppression, cancellation or persistent-buffer policies without target-specific evidence.

Check completion while open, completion after close, completion after dispose and actual unmount cleanup. Observe modal value, write calls, publication and original-result delivery separately. Exercise run after close and multiple deferred completions to confirm unchanged invocation and completion behavior. If testing callback reentry, close or dispose from env.write and verify that subsequent publication is suppressed while env.returned still receives the result. Keep syntax results separate from behavioral evidence: VISIBLE_CHECKS.md states, "These checks are required after an Action but do not test business behavior."

Verify that suppressing modal effects preserves env.returned(result).

rules.body: Apply when delayed edits belong to a persistent document owner while the current view owns a subscription, and saving can synchronously navigate. docs/host-api.md states: "Document buffers are owned by the store BufferBank, while Badge owns only a live subscription." It also states: "A store listener may call navigation synchronously."

Capture the current document buffer when accepting an edit and enqueue its text there. Retain the original document identity and persistent buffer reuse across view retirement. TASK states: "Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet\ninterval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save." src/coordinator.js already binds each buffer's consumer with "trailing(env.timers,120,text=>env.store.write(id,text))".

Before a callback-capable save, snapshot and retire the consumed pending state so reentrant flushing cannot duplicate it and reentrant editing can create an independent subsequent burst. Reuse the existing utility's ordering in src/services.js: "const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };"

Capture the departing view and revoke its current ownership before saving pending work. Complete its clearing render before callback-capable saving, or recheck authority before any remaining visible effect. Clean up the captured subscription. After retirement returns, an outer open must recheck its request identity before installing its view. Preserve nested navigation, nested edits and successor rendering.

Preserve accepted text on its original document, independent pending state for different documents, buffer reuse, current-document status filtering and original rendering and payload semantics. docs/host-api.md states: "All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics." Preserve teardown integration in src/Workspace.vue: "onBeforeUnmount(api.dispose);"

Determine departure scheduling from the task and existing behavior separately from ownership. For this editor, flushing the captured departing buffer before retirement returns preserves synchronous store availability while allowing active edits to coalesce. Do not generalize this into a deadline for every persistent owner, cancel accepted durable edits merely because a subscription retires, or destroy the store-owned buffer during view cleanup.

Keep transient preview policy separate. TASK states: "The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change." Preserve src/services.js: "const task = trailing(timers, 40, query => publish({query}));" and "return {query: text => task.push(text), hide: () => task.cancel()};"

Check latest-only saving after the quiet interval, subsequent bursts and empty-string edits. With pending edits, exercise switch, same-document reopen, close, dispose and Vue unmount; check original-document persistence, buffer identity, captured subscription cleanup and successor presentation. Trigger nested open and close from both timer-driven and departure-driven saves, then check final navigation, rendered output and nested edits. Confirm preview delay and hide cancellation remain intact.

limitations: Content acceptance does not establish cross-task effectiveness.

rules.body: Saving or subscription cleanup synchronously calls host listeners that may open another document or close the workspace.

Capture the old view and remove its current ownership. Finish final old-view effects, such as clearing its display, before callback-capable saving, or check authority for effects remaining after callbacks. An outer open rechecks its request identity after retirement.
Nested open/close, nested editing and the new view's rendering remain authoritative. Disposal also cleans up captured resources rather than clearing objects installed by a callback.
Protecting only final view installation can still leave a later stale clearing render. Do not require every host to detach first; notification order follows the current contract.

Invoke open/close inside listeners for timer-driven and departure-driven saves. Check document output, subscriptions and nested edits after the outer call returns, through both direct calls and actual unmounting.

rules.body:
Apply when progress reception serves distinct visits and attempts, startup can emit synchronously, decoding may finish later, and history and presentation have different lifetimes. README.md: "Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file again does open another visit." README.md: "The feed object is shared by attempts and visits for that file. Its `start()`
method may synchronously emit cached data, and `decode(packet)` may return a
value or a Promise." Confirm the target's explicit display-order requirement before transferring freshness filtering.

Install panel reception before callback-capable startup, preserving later streaming and reusable sources. Original src/progress.js: "  feed.start();
  feed.target.addEventListener("progress", listener);" TASK: "A transfer with a warm progress source shows no initial progress until a later
packet arrives." Check originating subscription and visit eligibility before decoding each packet. Retirement must stop new admission during startup even when physical cleanup is not yet available. README.md: "One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: `start()` may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A `showProgress` callback may select or hide
another visit before `start()` returns, while its caller has not yet received
the returned cleanup handle."

Separate packet admission, retained history and visible publication. Bind admitted decoding to its originating file and attempt; retain its history effect on completion even after cancellation, hiding, replacement or disposal. Original src/progress.js: "    const deliver = frame => { record(frame); receive(frame); };" README.md: "`recordProgress` appends transfer history. `showProgress` paints the panel." Recheck visit authority after recording because host callbacks may navigate synchronously. Original src/queue.js: "      if (state.current === visit) state.showProgress({ fileId: visit.file.id, attemptId, frame });" Cancellation of an attempt alone does not revoke presentation of already admitted decoding while its visit remains current and its frame remains eligible.

For explicit full-frame freshness requirements, capture reception order before decoding or callback-capable processing. Scope publication ordering to the visit, spanning retries. Suppress an older completion from presentation after a newer-received frame has been published, while retaining both history effects. Recheck authority and freshness after the history callback; commit publication ordering before invoking presentation, which may reenter delivery. TASK: "Full
progress frames may decode out of order; do not allow an older frame to roll the
current display backward." README.md: "Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit." Do not compare numeric progress values or require suppression merely because a newer packet remains pending.

Keep the repair specific to panel reception and necessary lifecycle/freshness coordination. Preserve adapter interfaces and payloads. src/queue.js: "  return { fileId: file.id, attemptId, visitId, kind };" src/notice.js: "  state.showQueued({ fileId: visit.file.id, attemptId: handle.attemptId,
    visitId: visit.id, status: "queued" });" Preserve diagnostic startup ordering and live decoded-delta handling rather than applying the panel's bootstrap or freshness policy globally. src/telemetry.js: "// Diagnostics count live deltas only. A cached bootstrap is panel state, not a delta." Its existing sequence is "  feed.start();
  feed.target.addEventListener("progress", listener);" README.md: "It is not the panel and must keep its existing behavior while the panel defect
is repaired." This preserves that consumer's own bootstrap exclusion; it does not establish a new global classification of packets emitted by other users of the shared target.

Verify cached startup and later streaming, immediate and deferred decoding, newer publication followed by older completion with both history effects retained, and later-received lower-valued frames. Check ordering across retries and nested delivery/navigation from history and presentation callbacks. During startup, hide, switch or reopen the same file, then emit another packet before startup returns: retired reception must stop new decoding while admitted history remains retained. Exercise navigation during listener removal and cancellation, entry-bound retries, retired-notice suppression, repeated cleanup, disposal, independent workspaces, unchanged payloads and unchanged telemetry. TASK: "Preserve ordinary streaming, diagnostic telemetry,\nand subsequent uses." Treat syntax checks separately from behavior: VISIBLE_CHECKS.md: "These checks are required after an Action but do not test business behavior."

limitations: Content acceptance does not establish cross-task effectiveness.

rules.body: View subscriptions define document filtering, event payloads and retirement notifications. Historical cases include both removal before saving and preserving a departing view's opportunity to receive its save status.

Preserve document reads and presentation, original event payloads and filtering. If the host requires the departing view to receive this save notification, deliver it in that order before removal. If retirement immediately forbids UI effects, mark invalidity first and protect later output.
Preserve public and injected interfaces, exact text, store-generated status and revision semantics, and normal subscription release.
Do not force different cases' notification contracts into one cleanup order. Checking stored values alone can miss status-display regressions and subscription leaks.
Observe notification-versus-detachment order, events after retirement, filtering of other documents, reads on reopening, and document/status output after nested navigation.

rules.body:
Apply when a shared progress source serves distinct visits and attempts, startup can emit synchronously, full-frame decoding may finish later, and history and presentation have different lifetimes. README.md: "Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit." README.md: "The source is shared by attempts and visits for that file. start may emit cached
packets synchronously; decoding yields a full frame, immediately or later.
Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order." Confirm these premises and the target's display-order requirement before applying freshness suppression.

Register panel reception before invoking startup, preserving later streaming. Original src/workflow.go: "env.Call(\"start\",file.Token);subscription=env.Call(\"listen\",file.Token,callback)". TASK: "Restore the initial progress update without changing the public\ntransfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, or queue-record behavior." Make retirement effective during startup so subsequent packets cannot start new work through an obsolete subscription, even before the outer startup returns. Keep already admitted decoding separate from that admission decision.

When the task requires full-frame freshness, assign ordering at packet reception before decoding or callback-capable work. Scope ordering to the display owner, including attempts sharing one visit. After a newer frame has been published, suppress older frames only from presentation. Recheck both visit authority and publication order after audit callbacks; commit the publication watermark before calling the display sink, which may reenter delivery. TASK: "Full\nprogress frames may decode out of order; do not allow an older frame to roll the\ncurrent display backward." README.md: "A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset." Reception order, rather than loaded magnitude or completion order, determines freshness. Buffering every result until arrival order can be reconstructed is not required.

Keep audit completion independent of display permission. Capture the originating file, attempt and visit; retain the existing audit effect for each admitted decode, including completion after hide, replacement, cancellation or disposal. Audit before deciding whether to paint, then recheck visit authority and freshness because audit may synchronously navigate or complete another decode. README.md: "recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel." Original src/workflow.go: "deliver:=func(frame interface{}){;audit(frame);view(frame,order)}". A stale display frame still retains its history effect.

Coordinate ownership across callback-capable startup and cleanup. Publish cleanup ownership before startup callbacks can navigate; reconcile the returned handle without overwriting resources installed by newer navigation. Remove old resources from current ownership before canceling them, and recheck the navigation request after cleanup returns. Cancel captured retired resources and preserve repeated cleanup behavior. README.md: "One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: start may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A showProgress callback may select or hide
another visit before start returns, while its caller has not yet received the
returned cleanup handle." README.md: "Removing a listener commits removal before calling the host detach callback;
that callback may synchronously select, hide or dispose. Repeated removal is
inert. Host callbacks execute synchronously unless explicitly deferred." Preserve cancellation order from src/workflow.go: "h.CancelContext();h.Stop();h.Env.Call("cancel",h.File.Token,h.Number)". A provisional handle is an implementation option, not a required public API.

Keep an accepted retry bound to its entry visit and file across cancellation reentry. Cancel the previous attempt before enqueueing, retain the accepted command's record and attempt creation, cancel its resulting attempt if its visit has ended, and publish its queued notice only while that visit remains current. Original src/workflow.go: "v.Handle.Cancel();accepted:=v;h:=s.enqueue(accepted,\"retry\");if s.current(accepted){accepted.Handle=h}else{h.Cancel()};if s.current(accepted){s.notice(accepted,h)}". Preserve record-before-transport ordering, independent session counters and disposal. Preserve the exact queue fields from src/workflow.go: "entry:=map[string]interface{}{\"fileId\":v.File.ID,\"attemptId\":n,\"visitId\":v.ID,\"kind\":kind}" and notice fields: "map[string]interface{}{\"fileId\":v.File.ID,\"attemptId\":h.Number,\"visitId\":v.ID,\"status\":\"queued\"}".

Do not generalize panel reception or freshness changes to diagnostic consumers, introduce numeric monotonicity, extend queue records, or discard required audit. README.md: "The same source service also has a diagnostic consumer, Telemetry/
collectProgressTelemetry, whose existing live delta observations are separate
from the panel. Keep its existing behavior during this maintenance." README.md: "Queue records are {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}
unless a separate authorization adds byteCount from file.size." Conversely, do not transfer an earlier task's absence of out-of-order display requirements into a target whose TASK explicitly requires freshness protection.

Check cached startup and later streaming; immediate and deferred decoding; newer-then-older completion with both audit effects retained; and later packets whose loaded values decrease. Exercise nested delivery from audit and display callbacks to verify authority checks and watermark commitment. Navigate during startup, emit another packet before startup returns, and verify retired admission, cleanup, newer ownership and subsequent delivery. Complete admitted decoding after hide, replacement and disposal; reopen the identical file as a new visit. Exercise navigation from unlisten and cancellation, accepted entry-bound retries, retired queued-notice suppression, repeated cleanup, independent sessions, unchanged payloads and unchanged telemetry. These checks follow TASK's preservation and freshness requirements and README.md's synchronous callback model. VISIBLE_CHECKS.md: "These checks are required after an Action but do not test business behavior."

README.md: "A view can receive a result while open or after it has closed; the shell belongs to the application." docs/host-api.md: "Shell policy is independent from modal state; close is terminal for a modal instance."

Check the originating modal instance's current closed state when the notification continuation executes, before assigning its value or observing a modal write. Admission-time eligibility cannot establish eligibility after suspension. TASK: "A notification received after the alerts modal is closed still updates the modal's state. Fix the issue." Original src/Workspace.jsx captures "const admitted=!s.closed;" but performs modal effects under "if(true)". Its terminal boundaries are "close(){s.closed=true;}" and "dispose(){s.closed=true;s.disposed=true;}".

Preserve the open-modal sequence of value assignment, write observation and publication. Where an injected write can synchronously close or dispose the instance, check current closure again before the remaining publication. Original src/Workspace.jsx: "s.value=result.value;env.write(s.value);void 0;publish();". Attempt 1 uses a current-state guard before assignment and another after env.write; treat the latter as a defensive checkpoint, not evidence that synchronous reentry is a documented host guarantee.

Keep original-result completion delivery outside the modal-effect guard, so closure suppresses modal effects without suppressing successful operation completion. docs/host-api.md: "write(value) observes a state write, returned(payload) observes each operation completion." It also states: "Native callback return port corresponds to the original awaited run result." Original src/Workspace.jsx places "env.returned(result);" after the modal-effect block. Preserve env.notify(input) invocation, payload identity and the existing behavior when run is invoked after close.

Limit the change to modal notification handling. TASK: "Change only the modal subscription; do not migrate the application-shell subscription." Preserve snapshot shape, terminal closure and actual unmount cleanup. Original src/Workspace.jsx: "snapshot(){return {value:s.value,closed:s.closed};}" and "useEffect(()=>()=>command('dispose',[]),[])". Do not introduce request freshness suppression, cancellation or persistent-buffer policies without target-specific evidence.

Check completion while open, completion after close, completion after dispose and actual unmount cleanup. Observe modal value, write calls, publication and original-result delivery separately. Exercise run after close and multiple deferred completions to confirm unchanged invocation and completion behavior. If testing callback reentry, close or dispose from env.write and verify that subsequent publication is suppressed while env.returned still receives the result. Keep syntax results separate from behavioral evidence: VISIBLE_CHECKS.md states, "These checks are required after an Action but do not test business behavior."
